We need to use Mockito to mock Position or subclass? Since hasLoss() uses getProfit(). We can create a spy of Position and stub getProfit() to return custom Num mocks.

We cannot access private fields. We can create a subclass for testing? Use Mockito.spy(new Position()) and then when(spy.getProfit()).thenReturn(mockNum). For null profit, stub to return null and expect NullPointerException when calling isNegative() inside hasLoss(). Since hasLoss() directly calls getProfit().isNegative(). If getProfit() returns null, NPE will be thrown.

For special numeric values, we can use DoubleNum.valueOf(Double.NaN), DoubleNum.valueOf(Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY), DoubleNum.valueOf(Double.NEGATIVE_INFINITY). Ensure that isNegative behaves accordingly.

For custom Num where isNegative overridden to true for zero, we can use Mockito.mock(Num.class) and stub isNegative() to return true, also stub toString maybe not needed.

For isNegative throwing RuntimeException, mock Num and stub isNegative() to throw new RuntimeException("boom").

For getProfit throwing IllegalStateException or Error, we can spy Position and stub getProfit() to throw.

Add test for NaN profit: mock Position to return DoubleNum.valueOf(Double.NaN).

Add test for positive infinity: DoubleNum.valueOf(Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY).

Add test for negative infinity: DoubleNum.valueOf(Double.NEGATIVE_INFINITY).

Add test for null profit: spy Position and stub getProfit() to return null, expect NullPointerException.
